hook.text: Roman soldiers formed clubs where everyone paid dues. When a member died, the club covered funeral costs.

buildup.text: These collegia were mutual aid societies — pooling money to shield each other from life's worst blows.

discovery.text: Burial clubs are a direct ancestor of life insurance: pooled risk among a group of equals.

twist.text: Romans didn't call it insurance. They called it duty. The math was identical.

climax.text: Community risk-sharing is older than any corporation. Rome proved the model two millennia ago.

punchline.text: Pool the dues. Cover the dead. Simple math.

quiz.question: What were Roman burial clubs?
options: Mutual aid societies pooling funds for funeral costs
